blocks.zh: "You are always thinking of someone else. You've got me into vitamins after telling me to get into vitamins for like twenty months."
blocks.why: always thinking of someone else = Dan's observation—Emma is always thinking of others. "You've got me into vitamins" = Emma's care—she got Dan to take vitamins. "after telling me to get into vitamins for like twenty months" = Emma's persistence—she nagged Dan. "And I've been less ill and you don't even rub it in that it's the vitamins" = Dan's appreciation—Emma doesn't gloat. "You remember what our kids' friends like to eat, and you send brownies when a friend is sad, flowers when someone is ill" = Emma's thoughtfulness—she remembers details. "You are insanely big-hearted" = Dan's praise—Emma is generous. This is Dan's portrait of Emma: generous, thoughtful, always thinking of others. But then the turn: "BUT—can I say something honestly now? You might not like it. But sometimes, because you are trying to do everything, for everyone, sometimes you're exhausted for us." = Dan's honest confrontation—Emma's generosity comes at a cost.

blocks.quote: “Mentally you disappear—you wander away. Miles or Poppy will be telling you something, or I'll ask you a question and . . . you're just not with us—you're somewhere else.”
blocks.zh: "Mentally you disappear—you wander away. Miles or Poppy will be telling you something, or I'll ask you a question and . . . you're just not with us—you're somewhere else."
blocks.why: Mentally you disappear = Dan's observation—Emma is mentally absent. "you wander away" = Dan's description—Emma's mind wanders. "Miles or Poppy will be telling you something, or I'll ask you a question and . . . you're just not with us" = Dan's example—Emma is physically present but mentally absent. "you're somewhere else. In a conference room at a publisher's, or in a manuscript that has kept you up" = Dan's list—Emma is thinking about work. "or worrying about a friend's divorce or dreaming up a letter to force the council to reinstate the lollipop man" = Dan's list—Emma is worrying about others. This is Dan's honest observation: Emma's generosity and busyness mean she's not fully present with her family. "I've taken things off you, only to find you doing them anyway" = Dan's frustration—Emma won't delegate. "it's like you don't trust me to get it right" = Dan's hurt—Emma doesn't trust him. This is the letter's core insight: Emma's need to do everything means she's not fully present.

blocks.quote: “I know I can't ever take back what I did when Poppy was born but I've made up for it now, so *deep breath* you need to stop throwing it back in my face when we argue, because it hurts.”
blocks.zh: "I know I can't ever take back what I did when Poppy was born but I've made up for it now, so *deep breath* you need to stop throwing it back in my face when we argue, because it hurts."
blocks.why: can't ever take back what I did when Poppy was born = Dan's admission—he did something wrong when Poppy was born (he was absent/depressed). "but I've made up for it now" = Dan's claim—he's made amends. "so *deep breath*" = Dan's pause—he's taking a breath before saying something difficult. "you need to stop throwing it back in my face when we argue, because it hurts" = Dan's hurt—Emma brings up his past failure. This is Dan's vulnerability: he admits his past failure and asks Emma to stop using it against him. "I'm here, I'm present: I'm not going anywhere" = Dan's reassurance—he's committed. This is the letter's emotional core: Dan's honesty about his past and his request for Emma to let it go.

blocks.quote: “I love you so much, Emma Jacobs. Happy Thirteenth Anniversary. Not unlucky for me.”
blocks.zh: "I love you so much, Emma Jacobs. Happy Thirteenth Anniversary. Not unlucky for me."
blocks.why: I love you so much, Emma Jacobs = Dan's affirmation—he loves Emma. "Happy Thirteenth Anniversary" = Dan's greeting—it's their 13th anniversary. "Not unlucky for me" = Dan's humor—13 is unlucky but not for him. This is the letter's closing: Dan's love and humor. The irony (for the reader) is that Dan will die on Dec 3, 2021—he won't have a 14th anniversary. "I love you so much, Emma Jacobs" = Dan's love. The reader knows: there won't be a 14th anniversary. There will be one more day, repeated.
